title: Artichoke, Cannellini and Lemon Dip
description: Tender artichoke hearts and white beans blend into a spoonable dip with lemon and a little thyme.
equipment: Immersion blender and tall heatproof jug

ingredients.name: plain cooked artichoke hearts
ingredients.note: Tender unseasoned hearts. Trim any tough tips.

ingredients.name: cooked cannellini beans
ingredients.note: Use plain, unsalted and drained beans.

steps.title: Soften the artichokes
steps.text: Cover {artichoke}, {beans} and {thyme} with {broth} in the HexClad. Simmer covered for 6–8 minutes until the hearts mash under a spoon.

steps.title: Blend the dip
steps.text: Blend the warm mixture with {lemon} and {oil} for 1 minute, until loose and silky.

steps.title: Remove any fibers
steps.text: Press the dip through a fine sieve, scraping smooth puree from the underside.

steps.title: Adjust the consistency
steps.text: Scrape all of the mixture into the measuring cup. Add cold water a teaspoon at a time if needed to reach about 1 1/2 cups, maintaining a smooth spoonable texture.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Chill until cool, about 45 minutes in a shallow container. Spoon onto soft potatoes or serve alongside chicken.

notes: Yield: About 1 1/2 cups. One serving is 1/4 cup. Make ahead: Blend and strain up to a day ahead. The beans firm slightly as they cool. Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze in quarter-cup portions for up to 1 month. Stir in a teaspoon of water as needed after thawing. Fridge reheat: Serve chilled. Stir until smooth just before portioning. Freezer reheat: If already frozen, thaw covered in the refrigerator, then whisk or blend briefly and serve cold. Option A uses lemon. For gentler Option B, substitute water for the juice and add a little extra thyme. The dip is dairy-free. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/6 of recipe): 57 kcal, 2.9 g protein, 8.3 g total carbohydrate, 1.7 g fat, 2.6 g fiber, 15 mg sodium. The estimate covers the prepared condiment. Add separately served foods when totaling a meal. Fiber is estimated before straining.
